entries.title: Fire clinch playoff berth despite loss to Revolution
entries.summary: <p>FOXBOROUGH, Mass. —Matt Polster scored in the first half and Matt Turner made it stand up for the New England Revolution in a 1-0 victory over the Chicago Fire on Saturday night.</p><p>The Fire (14-10-6) clinched a second straight playoff berth in two seasons under Gregg Berhalter, despite the loss — thanks to Orlando City's victory over D.C. United.</p><p>Polster took passes from Carles Gil and Peyton Miller in the 26th minute and scored his second goal this season to give New England (16-10-4) a lead it never relinquished. It was the 11th assist for Gil and the career-high seventh for Miller, a defender in his second full season.</p><p>Turner turned away six shots on goal for the Revolution for his sixth clean sheet in 30 starts this season. He had two shutouts through his first 112 starts for the club with both coming last year.</p><p>Chris Brady saved three shots on goal for Chicago.</p><p>New England improves to 10-3-2 at home, while the Fire drop to 5-5-5 on the road.</p><p>Chicago has lost two straight following a three-match win streak.</p><p>The Revolution beat the Fire 2-1 in Chicago last month.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Chicago: At Atlanta United on Saturday.</p><p>New England: At Philadelphia Union on Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Stars hand Blackhawks first loss with Connor Bedard this season
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> have taken one step toward competitiveness, but they still have another big step left to take.</p><p>"To start the year, we gave up a lot of chances and didn’t create much," coach Jeff Blashill said Saturday. "Now we’re creating way more but still giving up too much."</p><p>That was certainly the case in the Hawks' 4-0 loss to the Stars. It marked their first defeat this season with Connor Bedard in the lineup and their first time shut out at home since Dec. 13 last season.</p><p>The Hawks probably deserved a couple goals that excellent Stars goalie Jake Oettinger refused to yield to them. They were actually credited with a 19-16 advantage in five-on-five scoring chances.</p><p>But they also tested Spencer Knight's goaltending abilities behind them too often — particularly on the penalty kill and during four-on-four play, which the Stars dominated. Stars forward Arttu Hyry eventually scored late in the second period and again early in the third to break the game open.</p><p>Hawks turnovers at the defensive blue line and failed dump-ins at the offensive blue line were a recurring theme.</p><p>"We just weren't crisp," Connor Bedard said. "I don't think we were in the right spots for each other.</p><p>"We want to play fast and fly the zone, but we've got to make sure guys have an easy out. We just weren't getting the puck out of our end tonight, and that's on the five-man unit; that's not on the 'D'-men."</p><p>Blashill admitted the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/10/16/blackhawks-connor-bedard-first-games-back" >Bedard-led top line</a> hasn't created as much in the last two games as it did in Bedard's first game back (Tuesday). </p><p>The Hawks' No. 2 center, Anton Frondell, also received a career-low 12:40 of ice time, with Blashill saying "he didn’t have the same level he's had."</p><h3><b>Regression to mean</b></h3><p>It's funny how hockey tends to balance things out over time. </p><p>The Hawks went 4-0-0 against the Mammoth and 2-0-1 against the Stars last season. Those were surprising records against two playoff teams that finished well above them in the standings. </p><p>Already this season, however, they've lost to both — by a combined 10-0 score.</p><h3><b>Long break</b></h3><p>The Hawks don't play again until Friday against the Canadiens, giving them five consecutive non-game days to rest and practice (three times).</p><p>"Honestly, if I had my druthers, we would just keep playing," Blashill said. "But we have these days, and we’re going to take advantage of them."</p><p>We'll see if Bowen Byram is able to return from his upper-body injury by Friday. Andrew Mangiapane, injured since the opening game, is expected to resume skating during this window.</p><p>Knight lamented that the World Series doesn't start until Friday, either. Since attending the Cubs' penultimate home game, he has been enjoying the MLB playoffs.</p><h3><b>Similar spots</b></h3><p>Although Blashill clearly prefers Ethan Del Mastro to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/10/17/blackhawks-kevin-korchinski-purgatory-jeff-blashill" >Kevin Korchinski</a> as a defensive fill-in option, the latter is still somewhat in flux, too.</p><p>"Me and Kevin have been talking through the last month or so [about being in] similar spots at similar age," Del Mastro said Saturday. "Every time we're not in together, that's an opportunity for us to work on stuff. It's not often you get two 'D' to be able to work on stuff; it's usually two forwards and a 'D.'"</p><p>The 23-year-old defenseman has worked on his gap control, refining his decision-making process about when to step up and when to back off opposing forwards skating through the neutral zone.</p><p>His physicality can be valuable in the defensive zone, and Blashill likes how his confidence never wavers, no matter what. But his breakouts have long been a weakness, just like they've been for the Hawks as a team.</p><p>"For me, [breakouts are about] trying to keep it simple, not over-complicate things, stick to the script," he said. "It goes so fast; not everyone is in the right spots all the time. Knowing when to make a play and when to live another day, that's another big thing."</p>

"And it might make us practice harder and take care of the details more. Hopefully they get a bad feeling in their mouth and clean it with hard work and preparation and see what happens."</p><p>The Ramblers never got their running game going against Mount Carmel, and the Loyola defense looked overmatched against the Caravan's very talented receivers.</p><p>"Mount Carmel is too fast for us to be slow in our reads and our eyes," Holecek said. "We have to be in the right spot defensively. Offensively, we can’t miss a block; we can’t have a mental breakdown or a bad route or motion we didn’t call. All of it is a good lesson. I’m sure it will be tough for those guys, thinking they were that good. But in the end this should be a good thing."</p><p>Some early playoff bracket projections had Mount Carmel and Loyola meeting up again rather early in the Class 8A bracket. It didn't work out that way. The teams would not meet up until the state championship game.</p><p>Loyola wound up with an easier path to Illinois State than Mount Carmel. The Caravan could face Marist, Sandburg, Lincoln-Way East and Bolingbrook. Loyola's likely route is Evanston, York, Maine South and Huntley or New Trier.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/10/17/instant-predictions-picking-every-game-in-the-2026-ihsa-class-8a-state-football-playoffs" >Instant predictions: Picking every game in the 2026 IHSA Class 8A state football playoffs</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/10/17/high-school-football-ihsa-state-playoff-pairings-brackets-illinois-2026" >2026 IHSA state football playoff pairings and scores</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><h3>The Red Raiders’ road</h3><p>Breaking down the 8A bracket, Huntley's road into the semifinals stands out immediately. The undefeated Red Raiders picked up the No. 2 seed and likely will not face a Super 25-ranked team until New Trier in the quarterfinals.</p><h3>Class 7A is loaded</h3><p>The 7A bracket is significantly stronger than 8A. Undefeated Normal is the top seed, and undefeated Hersey is the No. 2 seed. But the major contenders for the 7A title are East St. Louis and Brother Rice, and unfortunately, they could meet in the semifinals.</p><p>The Second Round features several excellent possible matchups: Hersey vs. Glenbard West, Downers Grove North vs. St. Rita and Brother Rice vs. Batavia.</p><p>St. Rita has been in and out of the Super 25 this season, but the Mustangs beat Glenbard West on the road and have the talent, the experience, and a favorable road all the way into the semifinals, where Hersey could be waiting. A 7A title game rematch between Brother Rice and St. Rita is a possibility.</p><p>But East St. Louis, which dominated Mount Carmel in the season opener, has to be considered the favorite, with Brother Rice a close second.</p>

entries.title: Notre Dame's last-minute drive comes up short in loss at BYU
entries.summary: <p>PROVO, Utah — Bear Bachmeier threw a go-ahead touchdown pass with 1:47 left and then No. 8 BYU stopped No. 2 Notre Dame at the goal line to preserve a riveting 28-24 victory Saturday night.</p><p>The thriller capped a wild Saturday in which five of the top 8 teams in the AP Top 25 lost on the same regular-season day for the first time, per Sportradar. Paired with No. 1 Georgia’s 27-24 loss to Auburn, the top two teams in the country lost on the same day for the first time in the regular season since Nov. 17, 2012.</p><p>Bachmeier ran for two TDs, caught another and had 224 yards passing to help the Cougars (6-0) beat the Irish for the first time since 2004. Preston Rex added 66 yards on 10 carries to help BYU start 6-0 for the third consecutive season.</p><p>After Bachmeier's go-ahead score, CJ Carr completed several clutch passes to drive the Irish (6-1) into Cougar territory, including a fourth-down pass to Micah Gilbert that put Notre Dame at the BYU 9 with four seconds left. His final pass fell incomplete in the end zone.</p><p>The Irish cut an 11-point halftime deficit to five going into the fourth quarter after scoring field goals following a muffed punt return and a failed fake punt by the Cougars. Jonaz Walton plowed across the goal line on a 3-yard run to put Notre Dame in front with 9:31 left.</p><p>Bachmeier led BYU into Notre Dame territory, but Jayden Sanders picked off a pass at the Irish 15 with 8:05 remaining.</p><p>After the Cougars forced a 3-and-out, Bachmeier drove BYU 55 yards in 10 plays and found Walker Lyons on a go-ahead 6-yard grab with 1:47 left.</p><p>Carr threw for 261 yards and Nolan James Jr. added 77 yards and a touchdown on the ground for the Irish. Notre Dame ended a 16-game winning streak.</p><p>Bachmeier used a combination of efficient passing and tough running to put the Irish on their heels early. He completed 72% of his passes in the first half.</p><p>BYU capped its opening drive with Bachmeier’s five-yard TD run up the middle.</p><p>Notre Dame took a 10-7 lead on an 8-yard run from James. Then Bachmeier punished the Irish defense on back-to-back drives. He caught a short pass from Kyler Kasper and rumbled 15 yards to put BYU back in front. Then Bachmeier dove over the goal line from a yard out to extend the Cougars’ lead to 21-10 going into halftime.</p><p>The Irish drove down to the BYU 5 in the final seconds of the first half. Carr fumbled while trying to spike the ball, and Isaiah Glasker pounced on it to help the Cougars maintain a two-score lead going into the locker room.</p><p>It was just the second turnover of the season for Notre Dame.</p><p><b>The Takeaway</b></p><p>Notre Dame: The Irish struggled to finish drives in the red zone, turning the ball over once and settling for field goals after twice starting drives in BYU territory.</p><p>BYU: The Cougars had a chance to go up 28-10 in the third quarter before a pick penalty by Kasper wiped out a 39-yard touchdown catch by JoJo Phillips. The Cougars then committed back-to-back special teams gaffes that let the Irish back in the game.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Notre Dame is at Navy on Oct. 31.</p><p>BYU is at UCF on Oct. 24.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Judgmental sister demands childcare commitment
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My twin sister and her husband are expecting their first child. I run a small business with my father. Although I work hard, neither of them seems to see or acknowledge my efforts. They consider me to be "sponging" off my father. They also disapprove of my relationship with my boyfriend because we have chosen to remain unmarried and not have children, although we have been together as long as they have.</p><p>Recently, they offered to hire me as their nanny three days a week after my sister's maternity leave is up so that they can continue working. My sister also asked that I think it over without consulting my boyfriend.</p><p>I told them immediately that I could not commit to — nor do I want — such a huge responsibility. I said I would help them when I could but that my life and schedule were too unpredictable to be their primary means of childcare. I am uncomfortable with being their employee when our relationship is already somewhat strained.</p><p>This made my sister sad and disappointed and her husband angry. He will no longer speak to me and says he doesn't understand why I couldn't do them this "favor" after all the help with garbage, snow removal and mechanical issues he has selflessly given me (which is true). Am I crazy to think that this seems a lot to ask of me and that I have a right to say no? Should I feel as guilty as they are making me feel? — <i>NO NANNY IN NEW YORK</i></p><p><b>DEAR NO NANNY:</b> You are not "crazy," so don't feel guilty for refusing to allow your sister and brother-in-law to push you into something with which you are not comfortable. That they would expect you to become their babysitter without first discussing it with your partner (legal or not) is somewhere between sneaky and presumptuous.</p><p>You say your relationship with your twin and her husband is "somewhat strained." Well, it appears to be that way because you sense a lack of respect from them. That is the issue you should straighten out with her. As for her hubby, he needs to understand that: 1. You are happy working with your father in the business, and 2. Removing garbage, clearing snow and dealing with mechanical issues are not remotely equivalent to devoting three days every week to taking care of a baby.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> There is a great guy around my age who works at a nearby restaurant. I really want to meet him, but he doesn't seem too thrilled when women hit on him, and he doesn't seem to date or have relationships at all. I heard he was recently seen flirting with a co-worker. How should I approach him? — <i>LOOKING FOR A WAY IN</i></p><p><b>DEAR LOOKING:</b> You should not approach him. Attractive service industry workers get a lot of unwanted attention, and you already know that this man does not welcome the amorous advances of his customers. His romantic life is none of your business, so please stop poking around and move on.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams completes first 12 passes in 1st game back from injury
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — Caleb Williams gave the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> an opening drive that was worth waiting three weeks for.</p><p>The quarterback marched his team to a touchdown in his first action since tearing his hamstring in Week 2. Williams' hamstring looked fine, too, as evidenced on his 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Colston Loveland. Williams stepped up in the pocket, rolled right and threw across his body to Loveland, who survived a hit at the goal line for the score.</p><p>Williams finished the first drive a perfect 6-for-6 for 64 yards. Loveland had three catches for 36 yards on the first possession alone.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Williams to Loveland for 6!<br><br>📺: FOX/FOX One <a href="https://t.co/xhA9gco8xi">pic.twitter.com/xhA9gco8xi</a></p>— FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) <a href="https://x.com/NFLonFOX/status/2111868321108779236?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>He led the Bears to a touchdown on their second drive, too, which ended with a four-yard D'Andre Swift run. Williams started the game 12-for-12 for 142 yards and a 143.8 passer rating before throwing his first incompletion of the game — on third down during the Bears' third drive.</p><p>Williams returned to game action Sunday after the Bears played coy about his participation all week. Coach Ben Johnson didn't even tip his hand about whom he'd make the second-stringer. The Bears named Tyson Bagent the backup 90 minutes before kickoff, with Case Keenum serving as the emergency quarterback. <br></p>

entries.title: Ready or not ... Bulls will begin the 2026-27 regular season this week
entries.summary: <p>This is the time of the NBA season where almost every player and coach admittedly is filled with a certain amount of optimism.</p><p>Obviously, some far more than others.</p><p>Bulls guard Josh Giddey?</p><p>Get back to him in a few months after this roster has possibly been punched in the face and gone through adversity.</p><p>It’s not that Giddey is a cup-half-empty guy, but he is a realist. And the reality of the situation is he’s entering his third season with the franchise, has gone through a front office purge, a coaching change, and has seen enough player movement where name tags should be made available.</p><p>“Every team coming out of training camp probably thinks they’re going to surprise people,” Giddey said now that the preseason has ended. “Every team probably says the same thing, that they’re ready for a big year, but you never really know until the season starts.</p><p>“I’m very confident with the guys we have, but until you go through adversity, until you go through a losing streak, that’s when you find out where you are as a team. I don’t want to say we’re going to be a playoff team or whatever, but I think we’re good enough to be competitive every night.”</p><p>Las Vegas says otherwise, putting the win-share for the Bulls at 29.5. Understandable, but also a number that hasn’t gone unnoticed.</p><p>“Vegas does their job putting win shares out there, but it’s our job to go out there and try and win all 82 games,” Giddey said. “We’ll see where we end up after all 82 games.”</p><p>But that’s the thing about this season for the Bulls: They could end up with 29 wins but if rookie Caleb Wilson and third-year forward Matas Buzelis take major steps towards resembling foundation pieces for the franchise moving forward, it could very much feel like a successful campaign.</p><p>Just don’t try convincing Wilson that under 30 wins is an acceptable outcome.</p><p>“Honestly, nobody really cares on this team what Vegas says,” Wilson said. “We know that winning is a process, we know what it takes to win, so we just got to go out and do it. Of course we have that chip on our shoulder being underrated, especially in a stacked East (Eastern Conference), but we’re just going to take it day by day.”</p><p>A mindset Wilson has been practicing since training camp started. With five preseason games under his belt, the No. 4 overall pick finished averaging 15.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 2.8 assists with three blocks. He shot 43.5% from the field and 31% from three-point range but will start the regular season insisting that the game has already slowed down for him while his confidence hasn’t.</p><p>“I feel like I’m able to read defenses much better,” Wilson said of his improvement. “Offensively, I feel like I’ve gotten much better off ball. I’ve just grown in a lot of areas just through trial and error.</p><p>“I’m looking forward to competing, honestly. That’s all I really want to do. When the games actually matter, and everything matters, you get the best out of everybody. I’m excited for that aspect of the game.”</p><p>As far as new coach Tiago Splitter’s excitement level? Is any NBA coach ever really truly happy with the amount of work done in the preseason?</p><p>“All of the coaches on all 30 teams, they always think they gotta do more (in the preseason),” Splitter said. “We’ve got a checklist of things you want to implement, but it’s almost impossible. There are things that we’re going to implement throughout the season, defensively, offensively, also like game situations depending on who you are playing against, defensive schemes, so yeah, we’re not there yet, 100% we’re not there.”</p>

entries.title: Humboldt Park man charged with murder in September fatal shooting
entries.summary: <p>A Humboldt Park man was charged with first-degree murder in connection with a fatal shooting last month, Chicago police said.</p><p>Malik Nelson, 31, was arrested Friday in the Loop. Nelson allegedly shot 38-year-old Raymond Hammitte Sept. 10 in the 800 block of North Kedzie Avenue in Humboldt Park, according to police and the Cook County medical examiner's office.</p><p>Hammitte, suffering from gunshot wounds to his head, was taken to Stroger Hospital in critical condition. He died five days later, according to the medical examiner's office. </p><p>Nelson was expected to make his first appearance in court on Sunday.</p>

entries.summary: <p>A 16-year-old boy was outside in the South Chicago neighborhood when he heard gunshots and felt pain Saturday night, Chicago police said.</p><p>The boy, who was in the 7900 block of South Jeffery Boulevard at around 11:30 p.m., was shot in his lower back. entries.title: 4 injured in Austin drive-by shooting near Loretto Hospital
entries.summary: <p>Four people were outside in the Austin neighborhood when an SUV pulled up alongside them and someone inside fired several shots early Sunday, Chicago police said.</p><p>The shooting happened just before 2:30 a.m. in the 600 block of South Central Avenue near Loretto Hospital. A 45-year-old man, shot several times, is in critical condition at Mount Sinai Hospital, according to police.</p><p>Three others were injured and took themselves to nearby hospitals. A 39-year-old woman shot in her chest and a 30-year-old man shot in his neck and shoulder; both went to Loretto and are listed in good condition, according to police. A 28-year-old man shot twice in his face was in good condition at Stroger Hosptial.</p><p>Police have not announced any arrests.</p>

entries.title: 4 men killed overnight in Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Four men were killed overnight on Chicago's South and Southwest sides.</p><p>A 52-year-old man was found inside a Chicago Lawn home Saturday around 8:30 p.m. suffering from "injuries to his body," Chicago police said. He was taken from the home in the 2400 block of West 61st Street to University of Chicago Medical Center where he was pronounced dead.</p><p>Police are investigating his death as a homicide. No further details were reported.</p><p>Just after midnight Sunday in Little Village, a man was found unresponsive in the 2700 block of South Karlov Avenue suffering from a gunshot wound to his shoulder, police said. He was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.</p><p>In Greater Grand Crossing, a man was found shot around 1:25 a.m. in the 7600 block of South Cottage Grove, according to police. He was pronounced dead at University of Chicago.</p><p>About an hour later in Woodlawn, officers found two men suffering from gunshot wounds in the 6600 block of South Champlain Avenue, according to police. One man was shot in his head, and the other was shot in his leg. Both were taken to University of Chicago where the man shot in his head was pronounced dead. The other man, 20 years old, was in fair condition, according to police.</p><p>No arrests have been announced in any of the homicides.</p>

Edwards and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott. The Bears made offensive lineman Jordan McFadden and defensive lineman Jayden Loving inactive.<br></p>

entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Patriots top Jets 26-19 behind Drake Maye's 3 TD passes
entries.summary: <p>FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, New England overcame losing three offensive linemen and Charles Woods came up with Geno Smith's first interception of the season in the fourth quarter to help the Patriots hold on for a 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.</p><p>Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards in his third consecutive game with at least three TD passes.</p><p>Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry had touchdown catches for the Patriots (4-2), who have won three in a row. Douglas had a team-high seven catches for 86 yards.</p><p>A.J. Brown had three catches for 27 yards for the Patriots in his return from injured reserve, but his timing was off and had three drops on his 10 total targets.</p><p>New England won its fourth straight against the Jets and 19th in its last 21 meetings despite right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard Ben Brown (knee) leaving with injuries.</p><p>The Jets (2-4) had a chance to tie it in the third quarter, but the Patriots held them to a field goal. New York squandered another opportunity to cut the deficit to a field goal in the fourth quarter when Smith was picked off by Woods. It came on Smith's 166th pass of the season, ending his longest opening stretch to a season without an interception.</p><p>Smith finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards a touchdown to rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who had six catches for 103 yards in his return from IR after missing four games with an ankle injury.</p><p>New England's defense, which got a boost from cornerback Christian Gonzalez returning from a two-game absence with a shoulder injury, held New York to 0 for 3 in the red zone. The Jets were also 3 of 10 on third down and were stopped on fourth-down runs on consecutive possessions in the second quarter.</p><p>The Patriots led 17-3 at the half, courtesy of Doubs' diving 42-yard touchdown catch and a 9-yard scoring grab by Douglas.</p><p>The Jets trimmed the gap to 17-10 in the third quarter after Cooper got behind Patriots safety Craig Woodson and caught a 42-yard TD from Smith.</p><p>That remained the score when Jets edge rusher David Bailey stripped TreVeyon Henderson of the ball and Jamien Sherwood recoverer at the New England 36. New York drove to 10, but Smith was sacked by Elijah Ponder, forcing the Jets to settle for a 36-yard field goal by Jason Sanders.</p><p>The Patriots responded on their next series, capping a 12-play, 658=yard drive with a 7-yard TD strike from Maye to Henry, but Andy Borregales missed the extra point.</p><p>Just four plays later and the Jets down 10, Smith overshot Kenyon Sadiq on a deep pass that was intercepted by Woods.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Jets:</b> LB Kiko Mauigoa left with a thigh injury in the first quarter.</p><p><b>Patriots:</b> Doubs (shoulder) exited in the first quarter following his touchdown catch and didn't return. ... Moses favored his left ankle when he left early in the second quarter. ... Vera-Tucker left in the second with a hamstring injury and was ruled out. ... Brown had trouble putting weight on his left leg as he was helped off in the fourth quarter with a knee injury.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Jets:</b> Host the Dolphins next Sunday.</p><p><b>Patriots:</b> Visit the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears</a> on Thursday night.<br></p>

entries.title: How the NHL's proliferation of no-trade clauses affects the Blackhawks
entries.summary: <p>Trade-protection clauses formerly reserved for only the NHL's elite players have become ubiquitous league-wide.</p><p>A whopping 320 players this season have some type of no-trade clause (NTC) in their contract, per PuckPedia and a recent story in The Athletic.</p><p>That's an average of 10 per team. And since players aren't eligible for NTCs until they reach unrestricted free agent status — or the years of an extension that extend the date they would've become a UFA — that means more than half of all NTC-eligible players indeed have them.</p><p>"I think we've gotten past the way no-trade clauses were originally intended," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said in a radio interview earlier this month.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> have very much contributed to the trend. Bowen Byram and Patrick Kane both got full no-movement clauses (NMCs) in their new six- and two-year deals this summer. An NMC also kicks in for Connor Bedard in 2030 for the final year of his contract.</p><p>Alex Vlasic will have a 10-team NTC starting in 2028 (for his last two years), Spencer Knight will have a 15-team NTC starting in 2028 (for his last year) and Frank Nazar will have a 20-team NTC starting in 2031 (for his last two years).</p><p>Veteran forwards Tyler Bertuzzi, Teuvo Teravainen, Ryan Donato and Cole Smith all received partial NTCs that allow them to exclude between five and 10 teams each.</p><p>NHL general managers, including Kyle Davidson, give these NTCs out as sweeteners to convince players to sign, or in exchange for slightly reduced salary-cap hits. They've become almost expected.</p><p>The NHL will likely try to insert some NTC limits into the next collective bargaining agreement in 2030. In the meantime, the proliferation will continue.</p><p>For the Hawks, the biggest NTC-related challenge probably won't involve the NTCs already on their roster. Some of them aren't actually that restrictive, and they view many of these players as cornerstone pieces anyway.</p><p>Instead, the biggest challenge will involve convincing talented players around the league to not block potential trades to the Hawks with their own NTCs in the future.</p><p>The scrutiny surrounding NTCs, after all, ignited this summer when stars like Detroit's Dylan Larkin and Winnipeg's Connor Hellebuyck demanded trades but wielded their clauses to prevent their current teams from widely shopping them.</p><p>Larkin has been derided for initially indicating, per reports, he would only accept a trade to the Panthers, Golden Knights or Wild — despite having demanded the trade himself. That would've given the Wings extremely little leverage to get a fair return.</p><p>NHL stars are becoming increasingly aware of how much power they hold. They're also becoming increasingly picky about where they want to play — the same thing NBA players, for example, have been doing for years.</p><p>And it turns out they generally want to play for winning teams.</p><p>That's where things get tricky for the Hawks, creating a bit of a chicken-and-egg conundrum. The Hawks could use a few more high-end players to help them climb out of this rebuild and establish themselves as playoff contenders, but many high-end players will keep them on their no-trade lists until <i>after</i> they've done that.</p><p>That dynamic risks creating a phenomenon where today's good teams stay good indefinitely because good players keep forcing their way to those teams — and on the flip side, where today's bad teams stay bad indefinitely for the same reasons.</p><p>Improving from within could become the only way to shake and climb that hierarchy, and that's one silver lining for the Hawks. </p><p>Their plethora of prospects gives them a better chance of doing that than other franchises depending largely on external additions.</p><p>The Hawks could also benefit from Chicago being an attractive hockey destination aside from on-ice results, as well as from the skyrocketing salary cap potentially widening the payroll gap between wealthier and poorer franchises.</p>

entries.title: Miami takes top spot in AP Top 25 for 1st time since 2002; BYU is No. 2 after beating Notre Dame
entries.summary: <p>Miami is No. 1 in The Associated Press Top 25 for the first time since 2002, No. 2 BYU has its highest ranking since its 1984 national championship season and Notre Dame and Georgia stayed in the top five Sunday after both lost close games.</p><p>The wildest and wackiest week of the college football season so far saw five of the top seven teams lose — a first in the AP poll's 90-year history. Miami and BYU were the biggest beneficiaries of the chaos and were joined by Ohio State in a tightly bunched top three.</p><p>The Hurricanes took over the top spot from Georgia, which lasted one week at No. 1 after losing to Auburn at home. The Bulldogs were the second No. 1 team in two weeks — Texas was the other — to lose to an unranked opponent.</p><p>Miami survived end-of-game drama to beat rival Florida State in double overtime and stay unbeaten. The Hurricanes' two-spot jump made them No. 1 for the first time since the 2002 season ended in the national championship game against Ohio State.</p><p>The Hurricanes received 40 of the 70 first-place votes from the media voting panel and were just 22 points ahead of BYU, which <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports/2026/10/17/notre-dames-last-minute-drive-comes-up-short-in-loss-at-byu" >won a thriller at home over Notre Dame. </a>The Cougars got 20 first-place votes and were 26 points ahead of Ohio State. The Buckeyes got nine first-place votes and were well ahead of No. 4 Notre Dame and No. 5 Georgia.</p><p>Miami is the first No. 1 team from the Atlantic Coast Conference team since Clemson in 2020. Other than Clemson, there had not been another ACC team ranked No. 1 since Florida State in 2014.</p><p>BYU went into its game against Notre Dame as a 10.5-point underdog and came out with a 28-24 win to go 6-0 for a third straight year. Since their championship season 42 years ago, the Cougars hadn't been higher than No. 4 in a poll or in the top five since 1996.</p><p>Every single spot in the Top 25 has a new team this week, but only two teams dropped out of the rankings. A wholesale shakeup of the top 10 did not happen largely because Notre Dame, Georgia and No. 6 Indiana had built-up capital with their 6-0 starts, plus the losses by the Fighting Irish and Hoosiers were against top-10 opponents.</p><p>Indiana, which lost at home to Ohio State, was followed by Mississippi, Texas Tech, UCLA and Utah. Texas Tech received the remaining first-place vote.</p><p>Alabama's loss at Tennessee dropped the Crimson Tide seven spots to No. 13 and Texas plummeted 12 rungs to No. 19 after its home loss to Florida.</p><h3>In and out</h3><h3></h3><p><b>In:</b> No. 20 Florida, which dropped out last week after consecutive lopsided losses, is back after going to Texas and handing the Longhorns a second loss in a row.</p><p><b>In:</b> No. 25 Arizona, which had an open date, has four straight double-digit wins since losing to BYU and makes its season debut in the poll.</p><p><b>Out:</b> Oklahoma State's loss at Houston brought an end to the Cowboys' three-week run in the poll.</p><p><b>Out:</b> Mississippi State got bounced for the 31-0 loss at LSU that followed a 23-point home loss to Alabama.</p><h3>Poll points</h3><h3></h3><p>• The last time the SEC's top team in the rankings — it's No. 5 Georgia this week — was behind teams from each of the other power conferences was Dec. 3, 2023, when Alabama was No. 5 behind teams from the Big Ten (Michigan), Pac-12 (Washington), Big 12 (Texas) and ACC (Florida State).</p><p>• The last time the Nos. 1 and 2 teams lost in the same week in the regular season was 2017, when No. 1 Alabama lost to Auburn and No. 2 Miami lost to Pittsburgh on Thanksgiving weekend.</p><p>• The last time unranked teams knocked off No. 1s in consecutive weeks was 1990. Miami hosts unranked Pittsburgh on Saturday.</p><p>• No. 9 UCLA has matched its highest ranking since 2022 and No. 14 Houston has its highest ranking since it was No. 11 at midseason in 2016.</p><h3>Conference call</h3><h3></h3><p><b>SEC (9 ranked teams):</b> No. 5 Georgia, No. 7 Mississippi, No. 11 Tennessee, No. 12 Kentucky, No. 13 Alabama, No. 18 LSU, No. 19 Texas, No. 20 Florida, No. 22 Missouri.</p><p><b>Big Ten (6):</b> No. 3 Ohio State, No. 6 Indiana, No. 9 UCLA, No. 15 Iowa, No. 16 USC, No. 24 Northwestern.</p><p><b>Big 12 (5):</b> No. 2 BYU, No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 10 Utah, No. 14 Houston, No. 25 Arizona.</p><p><b>ACC (3):</b> No. 1 Miami, No. 17 Wake Forest, No. 23 SMU.</p><p><b>Pac-12 (1):</b> No. 21 Boise State.</p><p><b>Independent (1):</b> No. 4 Notre Dame.</p><h3>Ranked vs. ranked</h3><h3></h3><p><b>No. 7 Mississippi at No. 19 Texas:</b> The Rebels have found their footing after that 24-point loss to Florida, outscoring Vanderbilt and Missouri by a combined 83-20. Longhorns are reeling and might have a new QB this week.</p><p><b>No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah:</b> The Cougars have beaten one ranked team each of the last three seasons and will go for a second against an unbeaten Utah team that escaped Colorado as a 15.5-point favorite.</p><p></p><p></p><h3>The Top 25 </h3><h3></h3><p>1. entries.title: Bears' Ben Johnson was back in his bag in 'crossroads' win against Falcons
entries.summary: <p>Ben Johnson grinned wide in the afterglow of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/caleb-williams-leads-bears-to-td-on-first-drive-back-from-injury" target="_blank" >the Bears’ 31-23 win against the Falcons</a> and placed his right hand over his heart. There was only one thing left for a proud coach to do before completing the scene with a “Good, Better, Best” chant heard round Atlanta.</p><p>He bent his right leg at the knee and shook the thing like a lunatic.</p><p>A visiting locker room full of delighted twentysomething gladiators probably could tell you exactly what maneuver Johnson was attempting, maybe even put a name on it. Either way, a man doesn’t have to dance well when his team is back on the good foot.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> came out hot with the offense again in quarterback Caleb Williams’ hands, leading 14-0 after a first quarter so absurdly one-sided, the Bears outgained the Falcons 154 yards to three. They built a 28-7 lead and ended the game with better than a two-to-one edge in time of possession, hard to pull off even for the team that leads the NFL in that category.</p><p>A successful hook-and-lateral on the opening touchdown drive — Williams to Rome Odunze to Roschon Johnson — signaled how ready the mastermind of the Bears' offense was for this one. Calling for a D’Andre Swift run up the gut on third-and-goal from the 4 on the next drive — it worked like a charm, too — showed the coach’s aggressiveness in a different way, less flashy but loud and clear.</p><p>“If you could write a script,” Johnson said, “that’s what we would want to do.”</p><p>Of course, he’d done exactly that.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">A little hook and ladder to get the first down <br><br>📺: FOX <a href="https://t.co/3SZ5qzXNiw">pic.twitter.com/3SZ5qzXNiw</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2111867233592807850?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>If it was a bad look for Johnson when the Bears were manhandled 31-7 by the Packers one week ago — and it absolutely was — this was the second-year coach shining anew, his 4-2 team back in the business of looking playoff worthy.</p><p>“I’m not surprised whatsoever,” he said. “It’s kind of been the history of those guys in that locker room. We get punched in the face, and they want to come back and make sure we get everything fixed, corrected and go on.”</p><p>Johnson needed a game like this — on what would have been Mike Ditka’s 87th birthday, no less.</p><p>“It was one of those crossroads, if you will,” he said.</p><p>Now, he’s back to having a leg up — crooked and shaking, but up — on those who took shots at him after, and were eager to rub his nose in, the fiasco in Green Bay.</p><p>Things happen fast in the NFL. The Bears have to do it all again Thursday at Soldier Field against the Patriots, the reigning champs of the AFC. The dance continues.</p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>Caleb’s Hamstring Update: </b>When has he ever declined an opportunity to fill in the evil media before?</p><p><b>Who’s Toting the Rock? </b>Nothing would give the Bears a positive jolt more than the return of Kyle Monagai from a turf toe. And will Swift be able to go against the Pats?</p><p><b>Is Flash Gordon the Key on D? </b>Having him out there again really gets the imagination revving.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-falcons-grades-caleb-williams-kyler-gordon-colston-loveland-chicago-atlanta-nfl" >Bears’ grades are in. entries.title: Bears notebook: Coach Ben Johnson won't do anything 'rash' in response to pile of penalties vs. Falcons
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — It ended up being a footnote on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-cb-kyler-gordon-goes-off-with-3-sacks-in-return-from-injury-everything-i-wanted" target="_blank" >the Bears’ 31-23 win over the Falcons</a> on Sunday, but they piled up an absurd 133 yards in penalties — their most in a decade.</p><p>At the center of that mess was wide receiver Jahdae Walker, who had as bad of a game as possible in that department and eventually was ejected.</p><p>Walker committed an egregious error early in the third quarter with an obvious running-into-the punter penalty that allowed the Falcons to keep the ball after the Bears’ defense had gotten a stop on third-and-three. Coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/16/bears-coach-ben-johnson-is-not-here-merely-to-win-we-want-to-be-feared" >Ben Johnson</a> just stared at the roof as the official announced the penalty</p><p>Instead of punting, they got a first down at the Bears’ 35-yard line. Walker was fortunate the defense bailed him out with a fourth-down stop a few plays later.</p><p>No one could help Walker, however, when he messed up again at the start of the fourth quarter. After a Bears kickoff, Walker got into it with Falcons wide receiver Chris Blair and headbutted him. That drew a 15-yard penalty and an ejection, and when the official explained that one to Johnson, the coach appeared to say, “Yep,” and moved on.</p><p>The penalty yardage total was the Bears’ highest since a 2016 loss to the Lions and among the 20 highest in franchise history.</p><p>Bears tight end Colston Loveland got flagged for offensive pass interference penalty in the third quarter and wiped out a would-be fourth-down conversion. Loveland appeared to make minimal contact with safety Xavier Watts as he ran for a 10-yard catch.</p><p>Johnson was frustrated because he said the scouting report he gave the players on that officiating crew’s tendencies held true.</p><p>“We’ve got to be more aware of it and play cleaner football,” he said. “We had penalty issues early in the season and cleaned those up. I’m not going to let one poor game of that define us. You’ve got to see a streak of that before you do anything rash.”</p><h3><b>Trapilo returns</b></h3><h3></h3><p>There was a big moment for the Bears late in the second quarter as left tackle Ozzy Trapilo got back on the field for the first time since suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in his knee last season in the playoffs.</p><p>“You’re always going to be nervous, but then that first play happens and it all washes away,” he said.</p><p>Trapilo subbed in for starter Theo Benedet for one series and did fine until he committed a costly holding penalty. The Bears converted on third-and-seven on a 24-yard pass from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze, but it was negated by the hold.</p><p>Trapilo also got some snaps late in the game.</p><h3><b>Lesson learned</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Backup running back Roschon Johnson rushed for a career-high 51 yards and scored a touchdown, but also nearly blew the game with a fourth-quarter fumble.</p><p>He had a chance to score again in the final minute as the Bears were killing clock, but though better of it and slid at the 4-yard line to end the game.</p><p>“Coming off the fumble, I’m like, ‘I have to do what’s right,’” he said.</p><h3><b>Notes</b></h3><h3></h3><p>• The game was delayed 15 minutes or so in the third quarter when Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels hurt his neck tackling Loveland. He was immobilized and taken off on a stretcher, but was doing well and walking around the locker room after the game.</p><p>• Wide receiver Luther Burden led the Bears with eight catches for 95 yards.</p><p>• With defensive end Montez Sweat out, longtime special teamer Daniel Hardy played that position off the bench and got his first career sack. He called it “awesome” and admitted, “It’s been five years, and there were times when I thought it wasn’t coming.”</p><p>• Bears kicker Cairo Santos missed a 56-yard field goal wide left, but hit a 50-yarder in the fourth quarter.</p>

entries.title: Bears CB Kyler Gordon gets 3 sacks in return from injury in 31-23 win vs. Falcons: 'Everything I wanted'
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — Throughout the summer standoff between <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> and cornerback Kyler Gordon, there was always an underlying sense that they needed him. The defense came into this season with major question marks, and if Gordon was healthy enough to get on the field, he’d be an answer.</p><p>He was electric Sunday in his season debut, even while playing a limited role as he continued to work back into game shape. He charged up a defense that had gotten smacked around the week before and starred in the Bears’ 31-23 victory over the Falcons.</p><p>Gordon was dangerous on his very first snap, then ended the Falcons’ shot at a comeback when he drilled quarterback Michael Penix for his third sack with three minutes left. Penix fumbled, and linebacker Devin Bush recovered the ball at the Falcons’ 28-yard line to seal the win.</p><p>NFL records showed Gordon to be the first defensive back ever to get three sacks and force two fumbles in a game. He might have gotten four sacks if Falcons running back Bijan Robinson hadn’t committed a holding penalty to stop him from reaching Penix on the second-to-last play.</p><p>It was an incredible, vindicating performance — “Everything I wanted,” he called it — for someone who had his name dragged through the mud over the past two seasons as four separate soft-tissue injuries kept him out.</p><p>“That’s just the nature of the world,” Gordon said. “I’ve got a pretty closed circle, so I don’t really hear things unless my friends tell me. On to the next.”</p><p>He took the high road, and most of his comments were pointed toward the future rather than rehashing the friction that built up at Halas Hall over the last few months.</p><p>General manager Ryan Poles said going into the season he didn’t know if Gordon would play again for the Bears, and coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/16/bears-coach-ben-johnson-is-not-here-merely-to-win-we-want-to-be-feared" >Ben Johnson</a> turned stern and wouldn’t say more than a couple words at a time about Gordon while he rehabbed.</p><p>Gordon wouldn’t answer whether he and the team now are on the same page about his health and training regimen, telling reporters to ask Johnson, and laughed to himself when Poles’ comment was mentioned.</p><p>“I can’t control what someone else says,” Gordon said. “I’m going to go out there and do my job to my best ability.”</p><p>Johnson couldn’t say enough about how he played Sunday.</p><p>He gave him a game ball in the locker room and said something indiscernible as he hugged him. He marveled at how much of an impact Gordon made despite the coaching staff limiting his on-field time — roughly 10-15 plays — as he returned from injury.</p><p>Gordon missed all of training camp and began the season on the physically unable-to-perform list, but has been practicing for close to three weeks. Johnson asked Saturday if he was ready to play, and he answered emphatically.</p><p>“He said, ‘Absolutely,’ and he sure enough was,” Johnson said. “Huge spark for us. He’s so twitchy, he’s very hard to block as a blitzer, tight in coverage.</p><p>“We’ve got to make sure we keep him on that right track. Those snaps he had were huge ones for us.”</p><p>Gordon made his season debut a few minutes into the second quarter at nickel on a third-and-four, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen had him locked and loaded for a blitz. When the Falcons handed off to Robinson, Gordon was in perfect position to dive at him for a one-yard loss.</p><p>He showed up again on blitzes twice in the third quarter.</p><p>On one play, raced untouched on Penix’s blindside to hit him as he threw from his own 2-yard line and force a fumble. On another, he fought through Falcons tight end Charlie Woerner to take down Penix as he tried to step up in the pocket.</p><p>“It was [like] a movie,” cornerback Jaylon Johnson said. “He came back after all the talk, all the chatter, worked his ass off and balled.”</p><p>When asked about Gordon getting more sacks Sunday than he’d had over his entire career, Johnson said, “He’s the best [nickel] in the league at it. He just has a different knack for the game.”</p><p>Gordon is just the 21st player in franchise history to get three sacks in a game and the first since former Pro Bowl defensive end Robert Quinn in 2021.</p><p>The Bears needed everything he gave them as their 31-7 lead slipped into a one-score game near the end.</p><p>They actually pulled their defensive starters with that lead in the fourth quarter in order to preserve them for their game Thursday against the Patriots, but had to send them back out. The Falcons scored a touchdown against the backups to make it 31-15, then scored again after running back Roschon Johnson lost a fumble with seven minutes left.</p><p>Penix’s late drives pushed his passer rating to 108.8 for the game, but the Bears accomplished their top objective by managing Robinson. Between jumping out to a 14-0 lead and some timely stops, they held the NFL’s leading rusher to 61 yards on nine carries.</p><p>Allen’s defense seemed to be turning the corner before the debacle at Lambeau Field last week, but maybe that game was an aberration in its overall trajectory. And if Gordon truly is back for good, he’ll accelerate its surge.</p>

entries.title: Immigrant crosses project honors Silverio Villegas González at parish he attended
entries.summary: <p>As churchgoers walked into Sunday evening Mass at Our Lady of Mount Carmel in Melrose Park, they saw a sea of crosses, including one of their own late parishioners.</p><p>The family of Silverio Villegas González, who was shot to death by a federal immigration agent in Franklin Park last fall during the Trump administration's massive deportation operation in the Chicago area, belongs to the parish, according to the Archdiocese of Chicago. His name appeared on one of the crosses.</p><p>"Obviously, a mixture of emotions of once again facing that reality," said Father Brendan Curran, co-founder of Priests for Justice for Immigrants. "A mixture of anger, frustration but also empowerment that there's something we need to do now is the time for us to raise our voice."</p><p>The names of people who had died in federal immigration custody or at the hands of federal immigration agents were etched on some crosses, while others read “never forgotten” or honored groups of people with the words “deaths of fathers at the border” or “deaths of suicide.” The project includes 103 crosses, counting all the people who have reportedly died in immigration operations since 2020.</p><p>The installation is part of a larger project called entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Falcons?
entries.summary: <p>Twelve <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> penalties for 133 yards? That’s way too much laundry.</p><p>Roschon Johnson’s fourth-quarter fumble? Instead of the Bears going in for the kill, it kept the Falcons in it.</p><p>But we’re just nitpicking here, aren’t we? Nearly everything else about <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/caleb-williams-leads-bears-to-td-on-first-drive-back-from-injury" target="_blank" >the Bears’ 31-23 win in Atlanta</a> was good. No, very good. And in some cases, darn near great.</p><p>Let’s get to the grades:</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACK — A</b></h3><p>Caleb Williams rolled left on his first snap in a month, hit tight end Colston Loveland for 16 easy yards and made a city rejoice. No, not Atlanta, though Bears fans did their best to take over Mercedes-Benz Stadium. No. 18 had 12 completions for 142 yards and a touchdown before his first errant pass, a wise third-down throwaway. A 30-for-36, 305-yard day was a thing of beauty. Adding next to nothing in the run game while protecting his all-important hamstrings was, too.</p><h3><b>RUNNING BACKS — C-PLUS</b></h3><h3></h3><p>D’Andre Swift scored twice but averaged only 2.8 yards per tote, then was held out in the fourth quarter even after Johnson’s fumble; he’s banged up, and the Bears play again Thursday against the Patriots. Johnson rushed 13 times for 51 yards and had two catches for 34 yards, a big outing for him. He was running free for the end zone with a little over a minute to go but gave himself up so the Bears could kill the clock, a selfless play that no doubt made up somewhat for his turnover.</p><h3><b>RECEIVERS — A-MINUS</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Luther Burden (eight catches, 95 yards) was everywhere. Loveland (six catches, 65 yards) got the Bears rolling with a bad-dude touchdown on the opening drive, holding on to an athletic grab at the goal line with cornerback Mike Hughes draped on him and safety Jessie Bates flying in with a heavy hit. Loveland wiped out two first downs with penalties and overran a route on which he could've scored easily, and rookie tight end Sam Roush had another false start.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colston Loveland in traffic for the TD 🤩<br><br>📺: FOX <a href="https://t.co/391AmEl7Qj">pic.twitter.com/391AmEl7Qj</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2111868248811520508?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 18, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>OFFENSIVE LINE — B</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Holding penalties would’ve been more damaging on a harder day, and Williams was sacked four times. One of the sacks was given up by tackle Ozzy Trapilo, active for the first time, and knocked the Bears out of field-goal position. Still, when big pushes were needed near the goal line, these guys delivered.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE LINE — B</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Bijan Robinson carried only nine times for 61 yards, an output with which the Bears had to be thrilled. Kentavius Street blew up a screen, James Lynch knocked down a fourth-down pass and a huge Daniel Hardy sack erased the Falcons’ chance to score before the half. Stretched thin, the wall held.</p><h3><b>SECONDARY — A</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Hello, Kyler Gordon — the nickel back, finally back out there after what seemed like forever, sacked Michael Penix three times and added a lightning-fast run blitz for a key stop. Is there a DB in the NFL who comes off the edge as savagely as Gordon? Elijah Hicks and Cam Lewis prevented possible Robinson touchdown runs with one-on-one tackles, and Lewis made a stellar fourth-down stop on receiver Zachariah Branch in Falcons territory. Dillon Thieneman blew in for a sack, great to see from the first-rounder.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — A-MINUS</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Punter Tory Taylor was on fire when called upon. Josh Blackwell’s recovery of Branch’s muff led to a touchdown that made it 21-7 at the half. Jahdae Walker, Zavier Scott and Blackwell were demons in coverage. Scott punched the ball out of Branch’s hands on a kickoff, with Nate McCloud recovering. Cairo Santos hit a 50-yard field goal but missed left from 56, and a potentially disastrous roughing of the punter by Walker in the third quarter was rendered moot when the defense rose up and kept the Falcons off the scoreboard.</p><h3><b>COACHING — A</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Williams re-entered the fray seamlessly. Even with Swift hurting and Kyle Monangai out, the running backs contributed. Despite injuries and Montez Sweat’s suspension on the other side of the ball, the defense came out more than ready. A very fine day for both Ben Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen.</p>
